entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner, minor represented by natural guardian mother under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 02.08.2019 the minor petitioner Shikari Meghana was walking on the left side of the road at about 2.45 on Mandya-Nagamangala Old Road near Kaman, at that time one Bus bearing No.KA-09-D-3355 driven by its driver with high speed in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came to extreme left side of the road and dashed to the petitioner and caused accident.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries on her right leg and other injuries all over the body.
Immediately she was shifted to MIN St.hospital, Mandya, after first aid treatment she was shifted to Pinnacle hospital, Bangalore where she underwent surgery and her right leg was amputated.

Petitioner has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines and conveyance etc.
3. That petitioner was hale and healthy before the accident and she was a student, now she is unable to concentrate on her studies.
She lost her right leg, she cannot do any work and also lost her marriage prospects.

That the petitioner's mother lodged a police complaint before the Mandya Central Police Station, and FIR is registered against the driver of said vehicle for the offence p/u/s 279 and 338 of IPC in Crime No.54/2019.
The 1 st and 2nd respondent are the owner and insured, 3 rd and 4th respondents are the insurers of offending vehicle.
They are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds she prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest @ 12% p.a and other reliefs in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 has remained absent on the date of hearing.
Therefore, he is placed ex-parte.
5. Respondent no.2 appeared through their counsel but not filed written statement.
6. Respondent no. 3 and 4 Insurance company filed common written statement and admitted the insurance policy in respect of Bus bearing No.KA-09-D-3355.

It denied the manner of accident alleged by the petitioner and contended that the accident was caused due to carelessness of the petitioner herself as she crossed the road unmindful of traffic, but not due to the fault of the driver of the bus.
That the police with undue influence and without proper investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the bus.

That the owner of the bus 1st respondent herein knowingly and Shikari Meghana vs Prema on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140721835/
2 willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not had a valid and effective driving licence to drive the bus as on the date of alleged accident.
Hence policy condition is violated.

The age,
occupation, income and permanent disability and medical expenses alleged by the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, this court has framed following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by the minor petitioner in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 02.08.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-09-D-3355 when it hit her while she was walking on the left side of Mandya- Nagamangala old road?
2. Whether the petitioner proves her age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
8. The petitioner is a minor, to prove her case, her mother by name Shikari Kalpana entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1, through her Ex.P.1 to P.15 documents are marked.
Doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.16 and 17 documents are marked.
On the contrary, Superintendent R.TO office, Mandya is examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.
R.1 to R.3 documents are marked.
The Administrative Officer of 4th respondent's company is examined as R.W2.

Through him Ex.R.4 to R.7 documents are marked, and respondent evidence is closed.
9.
Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
Counsel for respondent no.3 and 4 have filed written arguments.
In her chief examination she has reiterated petition averments and contended that the driver of the bus bearing No.Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-09-D-3355 was negligent in driving the vehicle.

In support of the same she relied upon the FIR registered by the Mandya police in Cr.No.54/2019 in which case is Shikari Meghana vs Prema on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140721835/
3 registered against the driver of the bus for the offence punishable under Sec.279,337 of IPC.

sentences.text: It shows one Nagamani has given first information to Mandya police on 02.08.2019 stating that she is the wife of one Manilal and she has one son and daughter.
That they are living in tent.
They belong to Hakki Pikki community.
That her daughter aged 6 years was going to the nearby shop to bring chocklates at Old Nelamangala road at 2.45 pm in the afternoon.
At that time, one private Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-09-D-3355 came in rash and negligent manner and hit her daughter.
The name of driver is Somashekar and the daughter of 1st informant is shifted to Govt. hospital, Mandya.
On the basis of said information received by Mandya police, Crime No.54/2019 is registered against the bus driver.

After investigation charge sheet is filed against him for the offence p/u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
12.
The wound certificate produced by petitioner shows that she suffered crush injury to right leg and displaced fracture shaft of tibia, dislocation of ankle joint which are all grievous in nature.
She was admitted to Pinnacle hospital with history of RTA on 03.08.2019 the next day of accident.
As per the IMV report no visible damage found to the bus.
The road is 25ft wide and accident took place at 2.45 pm in the afternoon.
The driver of the bus could have seen the movement of child in the wide day light.
13. Driver and the owner of bus have not questioned the FIR and final report.
In the cross of P.W.1 suggestion that child was left unattended by the parents is denied by P.W.1.
In respect of her name it can be seen that in FIR it is mentioned as Nagamani wife of Manilal, but in chief examination she is shown as Shikari Kalpana W/o Manilal Shikari.
Even in the petition her name is shown as Shikari Kalpana.
Respondent disputed her name that she is not the mother of injured and she has no relation with the injured, but the aadhar card produced at Ex.P.13 shows her name as Kalpana.
In her cross examination she stated that after her marriage she is called as Kalpana instead of Nagamani, that in her husband's house she is called as Kalpana.
Though her identity is disputed by the respondent side she has stated that she is the mother of the injured daughter and relied upon her aadhaar card to prove her case.
There is no contrary evidence to disbelieve that she is not the mother of the injured.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court the objections of her identity is not acceptable.
14. On the respondent side no other evidence is placed to show that minor child was left unattended by her parents and there is negligence on part of the child or her parents in the accident.

Therefore,
in the opinion of this court petitioner has proved that the driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-09-D-3355 was negligent in driving the bus and caused accident due to which petitioner sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I hold Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :
In respect of age of petitioner, aadhaar card is produced at Ex.P.12.
It shows that she was born on 16.08.2013.
Accident took place on 02.08.2019.
As on the date of accident petitioner has not completed 6 years, but she had completed 5 years.
Hence, it is held that age of the petitioner is aged 5 years at the time of accident.
Since the petitioner was minor, there is no avocation which can be attributed to the petitioner.

But even in the case of accident to minor,
compensation has to be worked out in non pecuniary heads, including treatment, transportation,
attendant charges, pain and suffering and loss of amenities of life.

sentences.text: The petitioner being non earning member, for the purpose of calculation of compensation in respect of loss of future income due to permanent disability, the observations made in the case of Mallikarjun V/s The Divisional Manager, national Ins. Co. 2013 ACJ 2445 (SC) which is also observed in Kiran V/s Sajjan Singh 2014 ACJ 2550 (SC) has been applied in the present case.

entities.text: Mallikarjun V/s The Divisional Manager, national Ins. Co. 2013 ACJ 2445 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is observed that, appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to actual expenditure towards treatment, attendant etc should be if disability is above 10% to 30% of the whole body Rs.3,00,000/-, upto 60% Rs.4,00,000/- up to 90% Rs.5,00,000/- and above 90% it shall be Rs.6,00,000/- and upto 10% it should be Rs.1,00,000/- unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
17.
To prove permanent disability petitioner got examined a doctor by name Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2.
He deposed that, petitioner has permanent disability of 70% of whole body.
He is cross examined by 2nd respondent and the material suggestions to P.W.2 are denied.
The suggestion that, the said disability will not come in the way of day to day activities and study of minor petitioner is denied by the doctor.

Having considered the evidence of the doctor, petitioner's right leg being amputated,
considering her photographs and other documents, this court is of the opinion that the permanent disability of the minor petitioner is 70%.
Accordingly, I hold Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.3:
In view of above reasons injury sustained by the petitioner is due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver and she is entitled for compensation.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and she was in hospital underwent operation and amputation of right leg.
She was advised to take complete rest, continue medicine and to take follow up treatment.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohd Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain V/s Regional Manager- U.P State Road Transport Corporation, Civil Appeal No.9070-9071 of 2022 dated 09.12.2022 has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- for pain and sufferings when right leg was amputated and disability was 70%.

entities.text: Mohd Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain V/s Regional Manager- U.P State Road Transport Corporation, Civil Appeal No.9070-9071 of 2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same can be applied to the present case also in the opinion of this court.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- .
Accordingly same is awarded.
(ii) For Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.10 and 11.
They show that, she has spent Rs.1,69,545/- because of the accident.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 those medical bills are disputed, but no satisfactory material is forthcoming to disbelieve the bills.
Accordingly, it is held that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,69,545/- towards medical expenses.
(iii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was in various hospitals for treatment from 02.08.2019 to 06.08.2019 for 5 days.
Accident took place in the year 2019.

Since she was in hospital,
food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.

Considering the cost of living, and food,
nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.500/- x 05 days = Rs.2,500/-is awarded.

sentences.text: For Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 5 days, someone should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if her family member has taken care of her in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence attendant charges has to be awarded.
if per day Rs.500/- is awarded as attendant charges, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 05 days =Rs.2,500/-is awarded.
(v) For Loss of income during laid up period:
Petitioner was inpatient for 5 days and she was advised to take rest also as she has underwent operation.
Minimum 6 months is required to recover from such operation in view of grievous injury and she being minor, someone should have continuously looked after her till she comes out of the pain.
Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 6 months including in patient period.

Her family member has lost the income in view of injury to minor child in 2019 and therefore loss of income during laid up period is Rs.14,000/x 6 =
84,000/-.
She is entitled to Rs.84,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted to hospital from the spot of accident.
She took treatment at Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences and Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Heath and also spent money for conveyance.

entities.text: Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Heath
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Considering all those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
(vii) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2 functional disability of the petitioner is assessed at the rate of 70%.
and as per the Mallikarjun case judgment cited above amount Rs.5,00,000/- is awarded for loss of income due to disability.
(viii) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :
As per the evidence of doctor, petitioner cannot walk, she has to use instrument or she has to crawl.
Therefore she suffers pain and discomfort.
Meaning, she cannot lead the normal life as she used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of normal enjoyment of life of petitioner.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.
Under the said head she is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/-.

(ix) For Future medical expenses: P.W.2 has mentioned that for artificial leg cost is Rs.2,60,000/-
and this has to change as she grows.
At the time of accident petitioner is only aged 5 years and after her growth due to age if the artificial leg is affixed, it will have to be changed and she has to bear expenses.
The doctor has not submitted any estimation report in that regard.
Petitioner also not submitted any estimation from the expert in respect of artificial leg fixation.
However, petitioner will be in need of future medical treatment in respect of her injury.
Therefore in the opinion of this court, the expenses towards future medical treatment shall be awarded @ Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner.
(x) Loss of future prospect:

As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, even in injury cases,
loss of future prospect has to be considered.

In the present case, the on going through the evidence of assessed doctor and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is chance of loss of future prospect as well as marital prospect of the petitioner.

Unfortunately in the present case minor Shikari Meghana vs Prema on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140721835/
6 petitioner having lost her leg in the accident and below knee amputation had to be done, any amount of compensation cannot rectify the injury suffered by her.

sentences.text: Hence compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future prospect and also marital prospects.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

ii.

iii. Food and nourishment 2500/-

iv. Attendant charges 2500/-

 period vi. Conveyance charges 10,000/-

Total Rs. 12,68,545/-
Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.12,68,545/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road traffic accident.
19. Liability:

Respondent no. 3 and 4 have admitted the insurance policy of Bus in the present case,
but they have disputed the permit as on the date of accident.

To prove that there was no permit to the said bus, authorized representative of R-3 is examined as R.W.2 and RTO, Superintendent,
Mandya is examined as R.W.1.

In their evidence they stated that as on the accident 02.08.2019 bus no.KA-09-D-3355 had no permit and the vehicle R.C was transferred from Mysore to Mandya.
20.
It is necessary to notice that, in the charge sheet there is no mention about no charge regarding having no permit at the time of accident.
In the file there is one fee received receipt in the name of 1st respondent Prema regarding stage carriage permit showing Rs.47,952/- is paid at Mandya RTO in respect of the present bus.
Nothing is elicited in respect of the said receipt.
Accident has taken place in the year 2019 before the amendment.

Since no evidence is placed in respect of the receipt which is available in file regarding permit, respondent no.3 and 4 have not satisfactorily proved any fundamental violation of the policy conditions.

Theefore, in the opinion of this court respondent Shikari Meghana vs Prema on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140721835/
7 no.3 and 4 have to indemnify the insured and liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Hence, I answer this issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
21. ISSUE NO.4 :
Accordingly I proceed to pass following;
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation Rs.12,68,545/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.11,68,545/-from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.1,00,000/- will not carry interest).
The respondent no. 3 and 4 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.

After such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of medical expenses of Rs. 1,69,545/-
and future medical expenses of Rs.1,00,000/- in her favour and remaining amount of compensation shall be kept in FD in any nationalized bank in the name of petitioner till she attains the age of majority and she is entitled to receive periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.
However, petitioner will be in need of future medical treatment in respect of her injury.
Therefore in the opinion of this court, the expenses towards future medical treatment shall be awarded @ Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner.
(x) Loss of future prospect:
In the present case, the on going through the evidence of assessed doctor and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is chance of loss of future prospect as well as marital prospect of the petitioner.
